clue.text: He perhaps takes brief nap, producing most quantities of wind

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, an example of a gas

indicators.note: brief means the word for a nap is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off after lunch and turns out to be the windiest sleeper of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims SIESTA to SIEST. 'He perhaps' looks like a man but is the symbol for helium, a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of gassy: the one giving off more flatulence or windy talk than any other.

clue.text: A pet gundog's boisterous energy!

indicators.note: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A lively hunting dog has plenty of bounce.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is no letter; 'boisterous' signals rearranging A PET GUNDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an informal idiom for drive, vigour and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Evangelists popular with top cult turned up in part of Caribbean

parts.note: the SA is the Salvation Army, an evangelical Christian movement
in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the following pieces read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top, written AI
taken as written

explanation.surface: Missionaries join forces with a trendy upper-crust sect on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses AI and CULT together, giving TLUCIA. The Salvation Army is a Christian charity known for street preaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Lucia is an island nation in the Lesser Antilles of the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Passage which opens right into houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the word into goes round the letter for right

explanation.surface: A passage leads straight into the houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb: INTO houses R.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Mounting bus, happy to be getting around in India?

indicators.note: mounting means rising, so in a down clue the word bus is read upwards
getting around means the word for happy encloses the following word

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller boards a bus, glad to be touring India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' in a down clue means reading upwards; 'getting around' is the containment signal, while 'to be' is a link. The question mark flags India as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: India is the classic example of a large land mass within a continent, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Campaign pursued by Shelter and the Guardian

indicators.note: something pursued by another has the other coming behind it, so the shelter word follows

parts.note: a war is a military campaign
a den is an animal's shelter or lair

explanation.surface: A housing charity and a national newspaper team up on a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelter is a British homelessness charity and the Guardian a newspaper, which disguises both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is a keeper or custodian, someone who guards a place or people.

clue.text: A mostly slow witted but extremely open-hearted majority

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for slow witted is kept, losing its final letter

parts.note: dull means slow witted
tho is an informal short form of though, meaning but

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of open-hearted

explanation.surface: Someone is a bit dim but warm-hearted in grown-up life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DULL to DUL; 'extremely' gives OD from 'open-hearted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Majority here is the legal age of full adulthood, as in 'attaining one's majority'.

clue.text: 50% of 25 as a round figure

indicators.note: fifty per cent is half, so the first half of the answer at 25 is taken

parts.note: the clue number refers to the answer at 25 across

explanation.surface: Half of 25 makes a nice round number.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to the answer at 25-across, whose first half gives the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a flat circular shape, a round figure in geometry.

clue.text: On hill we pick every second flower

indicators.note: every second letter of the words On hill we is selected, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Up on a hill, we gather blooms one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword pun: something that flows, a river, here the African river.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads flower as 'one that flows', a river such as this great African one.

clue.text: Old washers can be rotated only in pairs

definitions.meaning: dated washing machines with a washing drum beside a spin drum

definitions.text: can be rotated only in pairs
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: containers like cans that turn round, coming two at a time

explanation.surface: Vintage laundry machines whose drums have to be turned together.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful description: tubs are vessels like cans, they spin, and a twin set comes as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: These were common household laundry appliances of the 1950s and 60s, now largely superseded by automatics.

clue.text: Bivalve might be articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word for might is said rather than spelt

parts.note: muscle is physical might or power

explanation.surface: A shellfish might have a hinged, jointed body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' tempts as 'jointed', apt for a hinged shell, but here it means pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible shellfish with two hinged shells, a typical bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Public sector employees rendering polite assistance

definitions.meaning: the government departments and the officials who staff them
courteous help, read literally as civil plus service

explanation.surface: Government workers are said to offer courteous help.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a state's administrative workforce and, taken word by word, means courteous help.

clue.text: Mental hospital got specialist doctor

indicators.note: mental in its sense of crazy or deranged tells us these letters go wild

explanation.surface: A psychiatric hospital has hired a consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mental' reads as describing the hospital but signals rearranging HOSPITAL GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathologist is a medical specialist who studies disease, often through tissue samples and post-mortems.

clue.text: 25, for example, supports 4 resolutely

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the figure 4 is spelt out as a word
twenty-five is five times five, a perfect square number

explanation.surface: A number puzzle: twenty-five underpins four with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' here is the number itself, not a clue reference, unlike in 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare used as an adverb means firmly and unwaveringly, standing solidly.

clue.text: As an artist I reenact my career

indicators.note: to career is to rush about wildly, signalling these letters run out of control

explanation.surface: An artist explains her work: I re-enact my life story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun meaning working life but is the verb meaning to rush wildly; 'As' is a link. Tracey Emin is a British artist famed for autobiographical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is a celebrated British contemporary artist, known for confessional pieces like her unmade bed.

clue.text: Part-own a Uruguayan island

indicators.note: part of the following words supplies the answer, a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone shares ownership of an island with a South American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part-own' reads as joint ownership, but 'Part' tells you the answer is a stretch of 'own a Uruguayan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the central Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Not engaging half of volunteers, poorly skilled

indicators.note: poorly means in bad shape, so those letters are rearranged
half of takes the first five letters of the ten-letter word volunteers

parts.note: able means skilled, capable

explanation.surface: Unenthusiastic about half the volunteers, who are badly trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first five letters of 'volunteers', and 'poorly' then rearranges just those letters; 'Not engaging' means lacking appeal, not unoccupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unlovable lacks charm, failing to attract affection or win people over.

clue.text: Triumphant leaders adopt standard flag

indicators.note: only the leading letters at the front of the word Triumphant survive, the tail being dropped

parts.note: colours, or a colour, is a regimental standard or banner

explanation.surface: Victorious commanders take up the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' keeps just the opening three letters of 'Triumphant'; 'adopt' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three bands, like those of France or Ireland.

clue.text: Girl regularly sick during school examinations

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of the word Girl, its first and third

parts.note: ill means sick
in means during, as in 'in the morning'
GS is an abbreviation for grammar school

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl falls ill during her exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a selective British secondary school, abbreviated GS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grillings are intense interrogations, rigorous questioning sessions like oral tests.

clue.text: Swindle short, wealthy old local Greek

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or cheat them

indicators.note: short means the word for wealthy is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A short con trick played on a rich old Greek resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks as if it goes with 'Swindle' but trims RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric was a regional dialect of ancient Greek, spoken by the Dorians of the Peloponnese.

clue.text: Doctor (qv) routinely putting words into someone else's mouth

definitions.text: putting words into someone else's mouth

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician's notes say to see a separate entry about speaking for others as routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' poses as a physician but is the rearranging signal for QV plus ROUTINELY; qv is Latin 'which see', a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventriloquy is the art of throwing one's voice so a dummy seems to speak, literally voicing another's words.

clue.text: Solicitor being over-legal

indicators.note: the word Solicitor is over, or covering, the answer, which lies within it

explanation.surface: A lawyer is being excessively legalistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-legal' reads as a hyphenated adjective, but the hyphen splits it: 'over' belongs with the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful, permitted by law; it is the opposite of illicit.

clue.text: Reportedly hide money

indicators.note: reportedly signals words as they are spoken, so the word for hide is heard

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store, a hide

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone is concealing funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' is a noun here, a hidden store.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is money in notes and coins.

clue.text: Assembly expelling posh type

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so the posh letter is removed from the assembly word

parts.note: a forum is a public meeting or assembly
U stands for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A meeting throws out a snobbish sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from 1950s British usage of 'U' and 'non-U'.
explanation.definitionFit: Form means kind or variety, as in 'a form of life', so it equals type.

clue.text: A second little boy coming back as a shape-shifter

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: coming back means the boy's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Abe is a diminutive of Abraham

explanation.surface: A little lad returns for a moment in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns ABE into EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism with no fixed form, constantly changing its outline.

clue.text: Reject elements of police state

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, members of the police
to claim is to state or assert

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the components of a police state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'police state' reads as one phrase but splits: DI is Detective Inspector, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to deny or renounce, refusing responsibility for something.

clue.text: Over-theatrical thespian's allowed a Shakespearean role

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An overacting actor gets permission to play a famous Shakespeare part.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is the title character of one of Shakespeare's most famous tragedies.

clue.text: Revised edition of Webster has new definition of "scattered"

indicators.note: a revised edition rearranges a text, so the letters of Webster are reworked

explanation.surface: A dictionary's latest edition contains a new definition for a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster is a famous American dictionary, which makes 'definition' feel part of the wordplay; it is a link pointing to the defined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestrewn is an old past participle meaning strewn about or covered all over.
